name: Wet-rice paddy fields, lower Yangtze
summary: Small dug-out rice fields linked by channels to water pits, built east of Lake Tai in the Late Majiabang period, are among the earliest paddy-field systems known.
description: Late Majiabang communities east of Lake Tai, at Caoxieshan and Chuodun, dug small field units of roughly 1 to 15 square metres and joined them by channels to deeper water pits read as reservoirs, which allowed tight control of water levels for rice. Fuller and Qin note that a paddy field at Chengtoushan in the middle Yangtze, of about 4400 BCE, is perhaps slightly earlier and of a different, embanked form.

impact.note: The source says rice spread from its Yangtze core after paddy systems developed but does not show that later Asian paddy farming descends from these lower Yangtze fields rather than the middle Yangtze, so reach is held at many societies of one continent; controlled water reorganised rice growing, and the stone ploughs of the Songze and Liangzhu periods followed in the same region.

date.label: c. 4300-4000 BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Two sites east of Lake Tai, of the Late Majiabang period dated 4300-4000 BCE, have produced evidence of ancient field systems.

evidence.supports: Two sites east of Taihu Lake of the Late Majiabang cultural period (4300–4000) have produced evidence for ancient field systems
evidence.locator: Section 'Yangzte pre-domestication cultivation and early paddy-fields', p. 95

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Whether Tianluoshan has excavated paddy fields, and their dates, was not checked.
The source reports a paddy field at Chengtoushan, Hunan (Tangjiagang culture, c. 4400 BCE) as perhaps slightly earlier; it has no record and its relation to the lower Yangtze fields is open.
A 2022 paper (MDPI Land 11(6):831) reports a suspected earlier paddy at Zhangwangzhuang in the upper Huai region; it was not read.
Whether paddy farming in Korea, Japan, Southeast Asia and India derived from the lower Yangtze system is not settled by the source read.

research.note: Fuller and Qin say the Chengtoushan paddy field in the middle Yangtze, c. 4400 BCE, is perhaps slightly earlier than those of the lower Yangtze and differently built, so these fields are not shown to be the first, and the source does not say whether the two arose separately.
